source: ADR-0002 D6/D7/D9 (fixed) + phase-0-5-slice-brief.md §2/§6 + slice proposal §1/§3 (TD-set, PROVISIONAL)

video.motion_blur_note: ADR-0002 D5/D7 amendment 2026-09-22: the render shutter is 0 and these fields describe the blur the compositor applies after the head is in place. A render WITH this shutter is produced only as the blur-fidelity reference (render_passes.py --blur-reference), never as a deliverable plate
video.status: shutter angle PROVISIONAL (TD); resolution fixed by ADR-0002 D6
video.samples_status: PROVISIONAL — determinism and noise measured on the real asset

still.resolution_basis: square so a panel crop in either orientation has ≥ 3508 px on its long edge (A4 @ 300 DPI, brief §4B) — PROVISIONAL until COMIC_LAYOUT exists
still.samples_status: PROVISIONAL — 4× the video count (proposal §6 machine-time formula)
still.dof: the camera's own DoF setting; chosen for the page by the TD at burst 1

sub_frame_samples.at: evenly across the shutter, open to close — every 1/16 frame at 180°
sub_frame_samples.amendment: ADR-0002 amendment 2026-09-25 (approved): three samples (open, centre, close) could not describe a laugh pulse shorter than a frame — every blurred reference sat 0.41-0.64 px from their integration along the motion on SHOT_002 1209/1210; nine exact samples against a nine-instant reference: 0.055 / 0.106 px

colour.ocio_config: ASWF OpenColorIO-Config-ACES studio config — exact file, version and sha256 in toolchain.lock.json once pinned
colour.grade: never baked; separate CDL/LUT after compositing

exr.container: OpenEXR multi-part, one file per shot per bundle
exr.overscan_px: UNKNOWN — set by TD on the slice
exr.compression_status: PROVISIONAL, TD may change; lossless only on a reference slice

socket_space.from_blender: X_s = X_b; Y_s = Z_b; Z_s = -Y_b (Rx(-90°), det +1) — proposal §3

scene_naming.socket_parent_rule: SOCKET_HEAD is bone-parented to the `head` bone, whose base sits at the boundary ring: the socket transform carries the whole head pose (neck bend + nod), which is why joints.json has no neck/head entry. Head and hair objects are children of SOCKET_HEAD, unskinned; the body's SOCKET_BOUNDARY ring is weighted 100 % to `head` so the seam follows (contractor Q3, 2026-09-15; the placeholder used `neck`, which only held because its head bone never moved on its own)
scene_naming.head_shell_rule: exactly one render-visible mesh in C_HEAD carries the SOCKET_BOUNDARY group — the head shell; eyes, teeth, tongue, brows are further meshes in C_HEAD, exported into default_head_rest.obj and the envelope but not into the ring; hide_render objects are ignored (contractor Q2, 2026-09-15)

head_lighting_rule: shadow-caster only: hero head and hair have ray visibility diffuse/glossy/transmission OFF, shadow ON, camera ON (ADR-0002 D2 amendment 2026-09-14)

default_head_deformed.rule: every render-visible mesh of C_HEAD evaluated at every frame and sub-frame offset, socket-local, float32 [frames, offsets, vertices, 3], vertex order of default_head_rest.obj; C_HAIR must stay within rigid_tolerance_m of its first sample (contract: hair hangs rigidly on the socket) or the export stops
default_head_deformed.consumer: QC only — the D7 round-trip re-projects this head (ADR-0002 D7 amendment 2026-09-17); it is NOT a HEAD_RENDER plus file: a head technology receives the performance track, never the default head's deformation
default_head_deformed.basis: the rest head failed a correct export at jaw_open 0.87 (contractor v01, frame 1100, 2026-09-16); rigid_tolerance_m equals rebuild.cross_platform_tolerance.numeric_abs, ~100x above the measured float noise of a socket child

exports.camera_local_convention: Blender camera: looks down local -Z, +Y up; exported as camera-to-world in socket space

transform_conventions.socket: similarity C·root⁻¹·T·C⁻¹ — the socket's local frame becomes socket-oriented (identity at rest; head asset authored Y-up, Z-forward)
transform_conventions.camera: left-multiply C·root⁻¹·T — local frame kept: Blender camera looks down local −Z, +Y up
transform_conventions.joints: left-multiply C·root⁻¹·T — local frame kept: Blender bone convention, +Y along the bone from head to tail, +Z bone roll axis
transform_conventions.alembic: Blender world space as written by Blender; apply abc_to_socket_matrix_4x4 from proxies.abc.meta.json to every point

exports.editorial_merge_rule: when state windows overlap, the NARROWEST window's editorial wins (sorted by width, widest applied first)

socket_boundary_ring.order: weight = index/count around the ring, ascending
socket_boundary_ring.rule: head and body rings: same count, same order; rest-pose distance between matched vertices is reported

exports.default_head_rest: every renderable mesh of C_HEAD ∪ C_HAIR at the rest frame in the socket's LOCAL frame (C · socket⁻¹ · object · v); placed by socket.json → matrix_4x4; the D7 round-trip re-projects it and the head technology reads it as the default head's geometry (envelope reference, ADR-0002 D1)
exports.camera_px_by_profile: camera.json → intrinsics.px_by_profile[<profile>] carries focal_length_px / principal_point_px / resolution_px per render profile; the top-level px values are for the scene's (video) resolution

beauty.motion_blur: off since the ADR-0002 D5 amendment 2026-09-22 — the layers are rendered sharp and the blur is applied after compositing; the profile's shutter describes that blur
beauty.extra_passes: Vector and Depth on every beauty layer — per-layer vectors are what the blur reads

data.motion_blur: off — Depth is unfiltered and Vector is unavailable with blur (proposal §1 rows 5, 14)

blur_reference.motion_blur: ON, at the profile's shutter — the reference the blur-fidelity gate compares the post-composite blur against (ADR-0002 Validation criterion 8). Never a deliverable plate: split_bundles refuses this manifest
blur_reference.extra_passes: none — Cycles produces no Vector pass with the shutter open
blur_reference.motion_steps: every object's Cycles motion steps set so that its 2^(steps-1)+1 time points are the exports' sub-frame samples (4 for nine; render_passes.blur_reference_steps, recorded as settings.motion_steps) — the round-trip integrates the same instants (ADR-0002 amendment 2026-09-25)

parts.name: HEAD_HOLDOUT
parts.note: the head+hair silhouette with the C_HAND_FG occluders shadow-only in L_HEAD (unoccluded by them): what the head layer must fill; occlusion by the hand is applied by PRECOMP_FRONT over it. C_BODY and C_ENV are holdouts in L_HEAD, so where the body or environment is in front of the head the silhouette IS cut — the round-trip excludes and reports those pixels. The visible (occluded) coverage is the object cryptomatte in the COMPOSITE bundle.

parts.name: BODY_SHADOW_RAW
parts.note: raw shadowed body plate; HEAD_SHADOW_MULTIPLY = BODY_SHADOW_RAW / BODY_BEAUTY is derived by the compositor script

parts.name: HEAD_HOLDOUT
parts.note: the head+hair silhouette with the C_HAND_FG occluders shadow-only in L_HEAD (unoccluded by them): what the head layer must fill; occlusion by the hand is applied by PRECOMP_FRONT over it. C_BODY and C_ENV are holdouts in L_HEAD, so where the body or environment is in front of the head the silhouette IS cut — the round-trip excludes and reports those pixels. The visible (occluded) coverage is the object cryptomatte in the COMPOSITE bundle.

parts.name: CRYPTO_MATERIAL02
parts.note: channel names keep Blender's layer prefix and the cryptomatte/* manifest attributes are copied onto the part — a Cryptomatte reader matches channels by the manifest's name

parts.name: BACK_MOTION_VECTORS
parts.note: per-layer vectors for the post-composite blur (ADR-0002 D5 row 14 amendment 2026-09-22): the body under the head moves differently from the front-most surface that L_DATA describes

parts.name: HEAD_MOTION_VECTORS
parts.note: the default head's own vectors; a per-order head delivers its own in the same convention

COMPOSITE_BUNDLE.motion_vectors_consumer_note: MOTION_VECTORS rows in bundle_manifest carry shutter_angle_deg and shutter_position; in the still profile the consumer is NONE (ADR-0002 D5 row 14 amendment). Since the 2026-09-22 amendment the video-profile consumer is the post-composite blur, and the per-layer BACK/HEAD/FRONT vector and depth parts are what it reads

lighting_probe.placement: at the socket position, hero collections excluded from the probe view layer
lighting_probe.frame: the shot's first frame (lighting is asserted static)

determinism.status: settings fixed and asserted at render; bit-exactness on Cycles/Metal is MEASURED, not claimed — see slice/README.md

HEAD_SHADOW_MULTIPLY.formula: BODY_SHADOW_RAW.rgb / BODY_BEAUTY.rgb, clamped to [0, 1]; where BODY_BEAUTY.rgb < epsilon the factor is 1 (no information, no darkening)
HEAD_SHADOW_MULTIPLY.semantic: the DEFAULT head+hair shadow (ADR-0002 D3 amendment) — QC baseline and negative control, not a per-order input

SKIN_ID.formula: material-cryptomatte coverage of HERO_SKIN_HEAD ∪ HERO_SKIN_BODY (all ranks)

PRECOMP_BACK.formula: everything behind the head with the default head's shadow applied = BODY_SHADOW_RAW (equivalently BODY_BEAUTY × HEAD_SHADOW_MULTIPLY); occluders are shadow-only in the body plates (template L_BODY rule)

PRECOMP_FRONT.formula: FOREGROUND_PLATE — occluders in front of the head with their own alpha; alpha-zero where none

derived.STATIC_PRECOMP: the ordered pair PRECOMP_BACK + PRECOMP_FRONT (ADR-0002 D5 row 13 amendment)

compositor.per_order_composite: PRECOMP_FRONT over (HEAD_LAYER over SEAM_EXTEND(PRECOMP_BACK)), premultiplied overs in scene-linear; HEAD_LAYER comes from the head technology, with its own body shadow multiply replacing HEAD_SHADOW_MULTIPLY in PRECOMP_BACK = BODY_BEAUTY × M_child; SEAM_EXTEND per seam_extend (ADR-0002 amendment 2026-09-24)

seam_extend.criterion: ADR-0002 amendment 2026-09-24, A1 (approved by the owner 2026-09-25): FINAL = FRONT over (HEAD over SEAM_EXTEND(BACK)) — in the precomp-reproduction test with the default head (criterion 3) and in every per-order composite, so the test tests what production does
seam_extend.why: the head and the body meet vertex to vertex at the socket ring (D1), so the body plate under the head's lower edge shows the open neck (the torso interior) and the head's partial-coverage edge pixels let it through — a dark line along the neck, measured on every frame of SHOT_001 v01 and SHOT_002 v01
seam_extend.operation: inside the head holdout (HEAD_HOLDOUT >= holdout_known_max) and within zone_px of the projected rings, the back plate (and, for the post-composite blur, its vectors and depth) is replaced by the body grown from the pixels outside the head, one ring of 8-neighbour means per step, extend_px steps; everything else is untouched; slice/seam_extend.py
seam_extend.rings: socket_boundary.json: head_ring_rest carried rigidly by the socket (socket.json centre samples, rest_frame -> frame) and body_ring_per_frame, both projected through camera.json's centre sample at the profile's pixel intrinsics scaled to the render (HEAD_RENDER_BUNDLE plus files); a ring that dips is followed
seam_extend.welded: only where the seam is closed: the head ring's point (carried by the socket) and the body ring's corresponding point lie within ring_weld_mm; where they are apart the master's own seam is open, the full render shows the gap, and painting over it would hide a master defect — those points are left alone and reported per frame (OPEN_SEAM). Measured 2026-09-25: the contractor's asset 0.000 mm on all 240 frames of SHOT_001 and SHOT_002; the template's placeholder (a rigid, unskinned body) opens as its head turns
seam_extend.visible_side: only ring segments whose both ends face the camera make zone: the outward radial normal (from the ring's centroid, in its best-fit plane) points towards the camera, or within ring_facing_grazing_sin of perpendicular at the neck's silhouette; the closed ring's back arc, hidden behind the neck, adds nothing (geometry, not the depth pass: no depth convention assumed)
seam_extend.seam_mixed_pixels: A2 is taken over the boundary band inside the zone where HEAD_HOLDOUT lies strictly within seam_mixed_coverage — the pixels where HEAD over BACK lets the back through; the whole band diluted the line about threefold (SHOT_002 1210 at 25 %: -0.040 over 783 px, -0.097 over its ~320 mixed ones)
seam_extend.units: render pixels at every scale — the edge that mixes with the back is the reconstruction filter's width, a pixel quantity
seam_extend.status: PROVISIONAL — the 2026-09-24 trial (slice/measurements/precomp_seam_edge_extend_trial.py) grew 4 rings into a 3-px dilation of the material-cryptomatte seam band (about 5 px from the ring) and removed the darkening on 16 frames of both shots; zone 6 px covers the 2-px band plus projection tolerance, 6 rings reach every zone pixel from the neck

precomp_reproduction_test.head_layer_default: L_HEAD.Combined — head + hair with body and environment held out and the occluder shadow-only (unoccluded silhouette)
precomp_reproduction_test.report: max abs error, fraction within each tolerance inside and outside the band, mean abs error outside the band, same-seed layer agreement away from the head, occluder-footprint check (PRECOMP_BACK holds body, not hand), epsilon-branch pixel fraction
precomp_reproduction_test.boundary_band: pixels within boundary_band_px of the >0.5 edge of HEAD_HOLDOUT or of PRECOMP_FRONT alpha (no wrap at image borders)

pass_rule.seam_criterion: ADR-0002 amendment 2026-09-24, A2: the signed mean of (composite - full render) over the seam band — the boundary band inside compositor.seam_extend's zone — must lie within +-seam_signed_mean_abs_max; a systematic darkening is a line and fails on its own instead of hiding in the band fraction. PROVISIONAL: -0.084 .. -0.225 without SEAM_EXTEND on all 16 measured frames, -0.026 .. +0.006 with it (2026-09-24). A frame with no seam band in view passes vacuously and says so
pass_rule.status: PROVISIONAL — placeholder smoke (64 spp, 10 %): outside 1.0, inside@5e-2 0.923, band 0.017; at 8 spp inside@5e-2 = 0.855 (FAIL) — the gate needs the smoke sample count or more; calibrated on the real asset at the conformant sample count
pass_rule.on_fail: COMPOSITE_ERROR, exit 2 — criterion 3 is a gate, not a report; the inside-band floor and the band cap keep an edge-localised regression from hiding inside the exclusion set

precomp_reproduction_test.measured_cause_of_error: MEASURED 2026-09-15 on the placeholder: per-layer Monte Carlo noise is ~0 (same seed, identical geometry → identical paths; the shadowed body plate equals the full render bit-exactly on 99.97 % of pixels away from head and occluder, max 1 half-ULP). Every pixel with error > 1e-3 has fractional head or occluder alpha: the residual is two separately filtered layers meeting at an edge, plus half quantization

compositor.head_layer_contract: HEAD_LAYER (default: L_HEAD.Combined; per order: the head technology's layer) is the UNOCCLUDED head+hair, premultiplied; occluders never cut it — PRECOMP_FRONT does

per_order.formula: FINAL = PRECOMP_FRONT over (HEAD_LAYER over SEAM_EXTEND(BODY_BEAUTY × SHADOW_MULTIPLY_ORDER)) — premultiplied overs in scene-linear ACEScg; SEAM_EXTEND per compositor.seam_extend

inputs.bundle: renders/<profile> with COMPOSITE_BUNDLE, derived parts and a PASSing precomp reproduction and round-trip (prerequisite gates, CLAUDE.md §6)
inputs.head_layer: <dir>/head.####.exr — one RGBA part, premultiplied, colorInteropID lin_ap1_scene declared by the head technology (no declaration → error, never assumed)
inputs.shadow_multiply: <dir>/shadow.####.exr — one RGB part in [0, 1] declared colorInteropID 'data', the ORDER head's body shadow factor from the head technology (ADR-0002 D3 amendment); the default head's HEAD_SHADOW_MULTIPLY is never substituted — that would be a silent fallback to the wrong head's shadow

gate.rule: unfilled: fraction of HEAD_HOLDOUT ≥ 0.5 pixels where the head layer's alpha < 0.5 — the layer must fill the silhouette it was asked to fill (head_layer_contract); multiply: any value outside [0 − slack, 1 + slack] fails — a display-referred or 8-bit shadow map would otherwise be clamped to 1 (no shadow) and pass, which is a silent fallback
gate.status: PROVISIONAL — identity run with the default head gives 0.0 / 0.0 by construction; calibrated at the bake-off
gate.on_fail: ORDER_COMPOSITE_ERROR, exit 2; frames are staged and nothing is left in <out> except a manifest with status FAIL

reported_not_gated.overfill_fraction: head alpha ≥ 0.5 where HEAD_HOLDOUT < 0.01, relative to the holdout area — a different child's hair volume legitimately differs from the default; the D1 envelope is the bound, checked by the head technology at the bake-off

per_order.output: <out>/final.####.exr (RGBA half, premultiplied, lin_ap1_scene) + order_composite_manifest.json with idempotency_key (order_id + bundle manifest + frame range + input hashes), input hashes, per-frame metrics, fallbacks: [] (none exist); frames are written to a staging directory and moved into <out> only when every frame passed
per_order.prerequisites: bundle_manifest.roundtrip.status == PASS and its exports.export_manifest_sha256 equal to the export_manifest.json delivered in HEAD_RENDER_BUNDLE plus_files (a bundle without plus files is not an order input); COMPOSITE_BUNDLE.derived present with every frame's precomp reproduction PASS

bundle_attributes.not_carried: everything else from the raw header (Software, RenderTime, cycles.*, Camera, Frame, Scene) — recorded by name in bundle_manifest, not copied
bundle_attributes.colour_rule: colorInteropID / oiio:ColorSpace: PREMULTIPLIED parts carry the source part's scene-linear declaration; NOT_APPLICABLE parts (mattes, ids, depth, vectors, multiply factors) are declared 'data' exactly as Blender declares its data passes — a colour-managed reader must never transform them

roundtrip.script: slice/roundtrip.py (Blender's Python: numpy + OpenImageIO; loads NO scene)
roundtrip.criterion: ADR-0002 D7 round-trip; brief deliverable H; proposal §4 (Q4)
roundtrip.reference: HEAD_HOLDOUT — the head+hair silhouette with C_HAND_FG occluders shadow-only (ADR-0002 D5 row 2); cut by C_BODY / C_ENV where they are in front of the head (see body_over_head); mattes, not beauty, so this tests the transform contract and not shading
roundtrip.reprojection: the default head as rendered — default_head_deformed.npy for the C_HEAD vertices (interpolated linearly between the exported sub-frame samples), default_head_rest.obj for the faces and the rigid hair — placed by socket.json, seen by camera.json, rasterised with the profile's pixel intrinsics (px_by_profile) scaled by the render's resolution_percentage; 4×4 supersampled box coverage

time_integration.video: the exports' nine sub-frame samples themselves (exports.sub_frame_offsets_frames), trapezoid weights — the continuous average of the path through them — against a blur reference rendered at the same nine instants (render_groups.blur_reference.motion_steps); ADR-0002 amendment 2026-09-25. Before it: 9 samples interpolated between three exported ones with equal weights, which a laugh pulse shorter than a frame defeated (0.41-0.64 px along the motion on SHOT_002 1209/1210)

metrics.p95_boundary_px: 95th percentile of the symmetric nearest-boundary distance between the 0.5 iso-contours of both coverage images upsampled ×4 (bilinear) — sub-pixel, not the integer distance of binary masks
metrics.iou: intersection over union of the ≥0.5 regions
metrics.mean_abs_coverage_in_band: mean |reprojected − HEAD_HOLDOUT| within 2 px of the reference edge (excluded pixels and their 1-px halo dropped); measured floor on the placeholder 0.018–0.021 at 4K (Cycles' reconstruction filter vs box coverage), gated

iou_rule.formula: iou_min = clamp(1 − iou_boundary_error_px_max × boundary_px / reference_px, floor, ceiling)
iou_rule.basis: IoU is not a framing-free number: the same boundary error costs 1 − IoU in proportion to the silhouette’s boundary over its area, so a flat iou_min is nearly free on a big head and harsh on a small one. Stating the threshold as the boundary error it implies makes it comparable with p95 and independent of the framing — which burst 2 changes deliberately (close-up ¾ → profile, a hand across the face, the head far away).
iou_rule.status: PROVISIONAL — measured 2026-09-19 on contractor v01/v02/v03, SHOT_001, at 25 % and 100 %: a correct export implies 0.022–0.054 px of boundary error; the rest head on an open jaw 0.11–0.39 px; the 3° yaw control 0.24–0.33 px; the 5 px translation 3.6–3.8 px; the 5 px growth 4.5–4.7 px. 0.15 px leaves a correct export ~3× of headroom and makes IoU catch the rotation control, which used to fail on the band metric alone — with the old flat 0.995 a 0.5 px translation passed the IoU test at 100 %

gate.scaling: p95_boundary_px_max and centroid_px_max are stated at the profile resolution and multiplied by resolution_percentage/100; the boundary threshold never drops below 2/4 px (two quanta of the iso-contour resolution, one of headroom). The IoU threshold is not scaled and needs no scaling: it is stated as a boundary error in pixels and resolved per frame against that frame's own silhouette (see iou_rule), which is what makes it the same test on a close-up and on a distant head. mean_abs_coverage_in_band_max does not scale either. A reduced-scale run is still a weaker test — the render must use a percentage that gives whole pixels on both axes (render_passes.py refuses the rest) and the positive control cannot discriminate below 100 % — and the report says so
gate.status: PROVISIONAL (proposal §4; band threshold added 2026-09-15 review round 2 against a measured floor of 0.018–0.021) — calibrated by the bake-off; the 1.0 px boundary value comes from Cycles' ~1.5 px reconstruction filter. Reviewed 2026-09-16 on the real head (contractor v01, SHOT_001, 7 video frames + 1 still at 100 %; measurements/roundtrip_v01_SHOT_001_review.json): values kept — undeformed floor p95 0.25 px / centroid ≤ 0.006 px / IoU ≥ 0.9997 / band 0.016–0.020; the gate catches 0.5 px translation or growth and 0.5–0.75° rotation, mostly through the band metric; iou_min is size-dependent (≈ 0.67 px of uniform boundary error at this framing) — a size-aware form is proposed for burst 2
gate.on_fail: ROUNDTRIP_ERROR, exit 2 — a master whose export does not round-trip is not delivered (ADR-0002 D7)

translation.rule: the socket is displaced along the camera's x axis by the distance that moves it 5 px at the run's resolution; the gate MUST fail on every frame — otherwise the metric is NOT VALIDATED and the script exits 2

rotation.rule: applied to the matrix and the quaternion of every sub-frame sample; reported as VALIDATED if the gate fails, NOT_VALIDATED otherwise. On the placeholder the 3° yaw sits on the band threshold (measured 0.053 still / 0.050 video against 0.05) through the faceting of the 48-segment sphere alone — a rotation-symmetric silhouette cannot validate it. The real head (contractor v01, 2026-09-16) validates it on every metric: p95 3.3–3.5 px, centroid 0.77–0.81 px, IoU 0.992, band 0.17 at 100 %; the gate catches yaw from 0.75° (measurements/roundtrip_v01_SHOT_001_sensitivity.*.json). At 25 % the margin is thin (band 0.052–0.056)

scale.rule: fx and fy are scaled and the principal point moved so the silhouette's centre stays put: a pure size error growing the effective radius by 5 px at the run's resolution (an intrinsics / depth class error — the class of the still-profile principal-point bug found 2026-09-15); the gate MUST fail on every frame, else exit 2

positive_control.method: the shutter-integrated result is compared with the centre-sample-only result on every video frame; --ignore-subframes writes a whole centre-only report
positive_control.rule: DISCRIMINATING when centroid or band difference exceeds min_difference; NOT_DISCRIMINATING is recorded, not failed — it means the head did not move enough across this frame's shutter to test the sub-frame data (the placeholder's SHOT_001 is such a case; the real asset's fast-turn window is where this control must read DISCRIMINATING)
positive_control.min_difference_status: PROVISIONAL — raised from 0.001 on 2026-09-16 (measurements/roundtrip_v01_SHOT_001_review.json): on v01 the static frame 1001 (0.001° per shutter) differs by 0.0018–0.0020 at 100 %, which read DISCRIMINATING against 0.001 while testing nothing; moving frames (0.26–0.41° per shutter) differ by 0.0136–0.0404. A frame that does not move reads NOT_DISCRIMINATING whatever the threshold — pick a moving frame to test the sub-frame data. **Resolution matters as much as motion (measured 2026-09-19 on contractor v02 and v03, SHOT_001):** the same moving frames that read DISCRIMINATING at 100 % (differences 0.0136–0.0404) read NOT_DISCRIMINATING at 25 %, where the difference falls to 0.0042–0.0045 against this 0.005 floor — the sub-frame motion is a quarter as many pixels. A smoke run at 25 % therefore never tests the sub-frame data, whatever frame it picks; only a 100 % run does. The threshold is left absolute on purpose: it is a coverage difference, and scaling it would hide that a small render cannot see this

roundtrip.deformation_rule: since 2026-09-17 the re-projected head carries the frame's facial deformation (exports.default_head_deformed), so a deformed frame is gated with the same thresholds and the test measures the transform only. History: the rest head re-projected against deformed renders FAILED a correct export at jaw_open 0.87 (contractor v01 frame 1100: p95 2.57 px, centroid 0.57 px, band 0.069, 605 of 649 missing pixels at the chin) and passed at jaw_open 0.19; loosening the thresholds on deformed frames was rejected (it hides transform errors of the same size), and the old flag (max |channel| > 0.2) marked blinks and mouth corners that leave the silhouette unchanged. The rest head is still re-projected on every frame and reported as rest_head_comparison (never gated)

reference_quantization.model: a Monte Carlo reference's alpha is k/n for n samples (every ramp pixel of Cycles' blur reference is, measured 2026-09-25), so where the head's shutter-integrated coverage ramps with gradient g per px its 0.5 contour is known only to ~1/(n·g) px: matte_metrics.reference_quantization_px is the mean of that over the contour, in px — the same unit as the IoU rule's boundary error. roundtrip.py --plan-reference-samples computes it from the exports before the reference exists and check_asset.sh renders the reference with enough samples to bring it to target_px (rounded up to samples_step, never below the plates' samples); the round-trip records it per frame and, when a frame fails on IoU or p95 within it, says so instead of blaming the export
reference_quantization.basis: SHOT_002 v01 1209 at 4K, a laugh nod 34-74 px during the shutter: against a 64-sample reference the correct export failed the IoU (0.99929 < 0.9995, 0.309 px of implied boundary error against 0.15) with the centroid at 0.054 px; the same exports, plates and code against a 256-sample reference passed (0.99970, 0.133 px; p95 0.50 -> 0.25). The estimate fits both with a constant residual of ~0.08 px (0.228 + 0.08, 0.057 + 0.08); target_px 0.04 keeps the reference's share at half of what the residual leaves of the budget
reference_quantization.status: PROVISIONAL — one frame, two sample counts; re-check on SHOT_003's fast turn

roundtrip.body_over_head: C_BODY and C_ENV hold the head out in L_HEAD (only C_HAND_FG occluders are shadow-only), so HEAD_HOLDOUT is cut where the body or the environment is in front of the head. The round-trip drops pixels where such an object's cryptomatte coverage ≥ 0.5 meets the re-projected head (dilated 1 px, so the fractional-coverage halo goes with them) from every sum; contour points inside them are not QUERIED while every contour point stays a TARGET — dropping targets too made a kept point next to a dropped stretch measure the distance to the stretch's far end (176 px on a 5 px perturbation, measured); the price is that a spurious re-projected contour inside the exclusion stays a target. The fraction is reported; a shot where that fraction is not ~0 is a shot-design finding, recorded per frame. The exclusion is bounded: a frame whose excluded fraction exceeds gate.body_over_head_excluded_fraction_max (half the head) FAILS before any metric is computed — a wrong export that places the head over the wall or the body would otherwise be excluded instead of failed (found by the plain-vs-posed negative test, 2026-09-15). Object classes come from export_manifest (head_objects / occluder_objects / holdout_objects) matched to cryptomatte manifest names exactly; instanced or library-path names are not handled and would be an explicit error on the real asset, to be extended then
roundtrip.hair_transparency: OPEN — the reference matte is HEAD_HOLDOUT's alpha and the re-projection is solid mesh coverage, so alpha-cut hair cards would read as holes vs solids and fail the gate for a reason that is not the transform. The slice's default hair is solid sculpted strands with an opaque HERO_HAIR (contractor Q4, 2026-09-15). How a head technology's hair handles transparency is its bake-off exam, not the slice's; before a card-based default hair is accepted the round-trip must compare the C_HEAD shell alone against the head object's cryptomatte, or carry the cards' alpha

silhouette.criterion: contractor ACCEPTANCE item 2в — the body under the clothing is removed and the turn leaves no see-through hole at the collar, the sleeves or the hem. Measured since 2026-09-17: on contractor v02 the eye-judged previews passed while a 574 px opening between the dress collar and the neck was open from behind at the maximum head turn (the dress collar is a circle that never touches the neck, so a line of sight enters over its rim and leaves through the front). Judged by eye the defect was invisible; the gate finds it
silhouette.excluded: C_ENV and C_LIGHTS are not linked: a wall behind the character fills every opening and hides the defect. The proxies are camera-invisible already. C_HAIR is not linked either (2026-09-19): hair is an open-edged asset that the head technology replaces (ADR-0002 D3), so a gap between strands, or between the hair and the collar, is not a hole in the character — and hair cuts both ways, since it can hide a real opening behind it. Measured on contractor v02 and v03 over 36 camera angles in both poses: with hair linked, 16 of 25 regions at the seam were gaps around the hair and the real collar opening was framed by it; without hair, v02 leaves exactly one region — the 237 px collar opening — and v03 leaves none
silhouette.materials: each render-visible object is given an opaque emission material of its own colour, so one render carries both the silhouette (alpha) and the objects bordering an opening; a transparent garment material would otherwise read as a hole

pose.rule: the rest pose and the maximum head turn relative to the chest that the slice asks for — an opening that only appears in the turn is still a defect. The bones are rotated in their OWN local frame, where +Y runs along the bone: a turn is a rotation about Y, about Z it is a roll. Measured 2026-09-19: the first version of this block said "z" and produced a 60° roll with 7° of yaw — it still found the v02 collar opening, but it was not the motion the defect was about, so the achieved rotation below is verified after posing instead of trusted

max_turn.rule: after posing, SOCKET_HEAD's world rotation must be this or the gate stops — it is what proves the pose is the turn it claims to be

pose.status: PROVISIONAL — 60° of neck + head is the guide of contractor/burst-2 TASK §5; re-measure against SHOT_002 when it exists

render.basis: geometry only: one sample and a 0.01 px box filter make the coverage deterministic and effectively binary, so the count does not move with render noise

region_of_interest.centre: SOCKET_HEAD, in the pose being rendered
region_of_interest.rule: the gate covers the head↔body seam and the collar around it — the slice's own boundary. The radius is measured from the socket to the LINE OF SIGHT through the region, not to its projection: a sight line that slips past the neck passes within centimetres of the socket whatever the framing. A region farther out is reported, never a failure — the gap between a hanging arm and the torso is an enclosed background region too, and it is not a defect. Openings at the cuffs and the hem are clothing quality, which the owner judges on the previews
region_of_interest.status: PROVISIONAL — measured on contractor v02 and v03 (1.4 m character) over 36 camera angles: the collar openings lie 0.040–0.070 m from the socket, the gap between a floating brow and the skin 0.147 m, the arm-to-torso gaps 0.19–0.35 m; 0.12 m keeps the seam and drops the rest. Re-measure on the master's own asset

pass_rule.status: PROVISIONAL — measured on contractor v02 and v03 at this resolution over the declared views in both poses: with C_HAIR unlinked the only region left at the seam is the real one (v02 237 px at the 60° turn, seen from yaw 150° / pitch −10°; v03 none), and the largest region outside the seam radius is 1070 px between a hanging arm and the torso. 50 px is the floor that separates an opening from antialiasing at 900×700. Calibrated on the real asset
pass_rule.on_fail: SILHOUETTE_ERROR, exit 2 — a hole is a defect that costs a re-render once it is in a master, not a report

cross_platform_tolerance.units: the same absolute tolerance for every exported number: metres for positions and vertices, unit-quaternion and matrix elements, channel values in [-1, 1]
cross_platform_tolerance.basis: MEASURED 2026-09-16 on the contractor's v01: the same build script on Linux CPU (bpy 5.2.1) and on macOS Metal (Blender 5.2.1) produces exports and bone matrices that differ by at most 1.3e-7 m / 1.3e-7 per element (float32 arithmetic order); 1e-5 is ~100x above that noise and ~50x below the smallest modelling change the contract cares about (the 5 mm rest-gap threshold is 5e-3)
cross_platform_tolerance.rule: a rebuild on another machine is EQUAL WITHIN TOLERANCE when every number of every export file, every proxy vertex at every sub-frame sample and every field of the canonical scene content lies within numeric_abs of its counterpart and every non-numeric field is identical; byte-identical files are EQUAL; anything else DIFFERS and fails. The tolerance is never applied on the same machine (rebuild_shot.py) where exports must be byte-identical
cross_platform_tolerance.status: PROVISIONAL — calibration set: contractor v01 vs its rebuild (one asset, one pair of machines)

post_composite_blur.criterion: ADR-0002 D5 amendment 2026-09-22: motion blur is applied after the head is composited, because 'over' of time-averaged layers is not the time average of the composite — under relative motion it drew a visible line across the neck
post_composite_blur.model: time-sampled layered blur: at each of K instants of the shutter every layer is forward-warped along its OWN vectors, the layers are composited at that instant (FRONT over (HEAD over BACK)), and the K composites are averaged
post_composite_blur.motion_path: quadratic through the positions the vectors point at and the current one: p(u) = u*(Dn - Dp)/2 + u^2*(Dn + Dp)/2 with u = t / vector_reach_frames (since 2026-09-25 u = -1 / +1 at the shutter's open / close). Measured 2026-09-22: a straight line over-blurs at the turning points of a laugh bounce (~6 frames per cycle) and lost to no blur at all on 4 of 13 frames

vector_convention.time_base: the shutter's open and close instants: the first pair points at the shutter-open position, the second at the shutter-close position (ADR-0002 amendment 2026-09-25, approved). The plates are rendered with the time stretched by 720 / shutter angle (render_passes.time_stretch, recorded as settings.time_stretch), which leaves the picture unchanged and moves the Vector pass from frame ±1 to the shutter's ends; the render manifest records settings.vector_reach_frames (0.25 at 180°), every blur call takes it, and plates without it are refused. Basis: SHOT_002 v01 1209 — a path through frame ±1 missed the true shutter ends by 6.2 px median at 4K and failed the fidelity gate at 0.057; through shutter-end vectors the same code reads 0.018
vector_convention.meaning: displacement toward that instant (the shutter's open / close since 2026-09-25, see time_base) in array coordinates (x right, y down) = (sx*v[0], sy*v[1]) for the previous pair and (sx*v[2], sy*v[3]) for the next pair
vector_convention.basis: measured on Blender 5.2.1 by warping a frame onto its rendered neighbours: these signs cut the error to 0.139 against 0.356 with no warp, while assuming the same signs for both pairs was worse than not warping at all (0.367). Re-measure on a DCC or version change - it is not documented behaviour

samples.rule: K = clamp(ceil(longest path in px / px_per_sample), min_samples, max_samples)
samples.basis: PROVISIONAL - at 3840x2160 frame 1090 has 57 px of path and K = 48 showed no stepping; below about one sample per 1.5 px the streaks become visible

workers.rule: processes over the shutter instants; 1 by default
workers.measured: 2026-09-23 on a 10-core laptop, a 4K laugh-peak frame: 8 workers took 271 s against 107 s with one. The blur moves hundreds of megabytes per instant, so it is bound by memory bandwidth and the extra copies cost more than the cores buy. Re-measure per machine before raising it
workers.determinism: each worker sums its own instants and the parent adds the chunks in a fixed order, so the picture does not depend on how many workers ran (measured below 1e-6)

post_composite_blur.hole_fill: forward splatting leaves holes where a layer stretches; they are filled by normalised 3x3 averaging over at most 4 passes, and the count is reported
post_composite_blur.status: PROVISIONAL - measured against a true 3D-blurred render on SHOT_001 1084-1096 (head error 0.0076 against 0.0175 for Blender's VecBlur and 0.0127 for no blur)

blur_fidelity.criterion: ADR-0002 Validation criterion 8 (amendment 2026-09-22): the post-composite blur must look like the motion blur it replaces. Measured against a render WITH the shutter open (render_passes.py --blur-reference) on the frames with the fastest motion
blur_fidelity.metric: mean over the region of the max-channel absolute difference, on a 4x4 box low-pass of both images. The low-pass is not cosmetic: the two images come from separate renders, so per-pixel noise dominates the raw difference

regions.head: the head layer's alpha > 0.05, dilated by 10 px

pass_rule.note: every measured frame must be within head_mean_max of the true blur. On a frame whose HEAD moves at least discriminating_min_path_px during the shutter (the 90th percentile over the head layer's opaque pixels of the distance between its shutter-open and shutter-close positions — since 2026-09-25; the frame's longest path over every layer made a blinking eyelid count, SHOT_002 1185) the blur must ALSO be discrimination_min_ratio times closer to the truth than both negative controls, which are built from the same seam-extended back as the blur - without that the gate would pass a blur that does nothing. A frame that moves less cannot tell the difference and is reported as non-discriminating, and a run in which NO frame discriminates fails: it proved nothing
pass_rule.discriminating_min_path_px_basis: PROVISIONAL - measured 2026-09-23 on SHOT_001 v01 at 25 %: frame 1090 travels 14.2 px and separates the blur from no blur by 1.52x, frame 1094 travels 4.8 px and separates by 1.22x, frame 1001 travels 0.3 px and separates by 1.00x. Scale-dependent: the same frames at 100 % travel four times as far

negative_controls: no blur at all (the sharp recomposite)

a doubled shutter — the same path twice as long, every layer's vectors ×2 (since 2026-09-25 the vectors reach only the shutter's ends, so a longer shutter is modelled by scaling the path, not by extrapolating the quadratic past the instants it was fitted to)
blur_fidelity.status: PROVISIONAL - measured 2026-09-22 on SHOT_001 1084-1096 at 25 %: the blur scores 0.0076 in the head region, no blur 0.0127, Blender's VecBlur 0.0175; the noise floor of the comparison is about 0.004. Re-calibrate on the real asset and at 100 %. Measured 2026-09-25: that floor was a reference rendered with the plates' own sample count, sharing their Monte Carlo pattern (static SHOT_002 1121 at 25 %: 0.003 from the plates); a reference with more samples — which the round-trip now needs on fast frames (roundtrip.reference_quantization) — sits 0.010 from the 64-sample plates and from the same-count reference alike, so the honest floor at the video profile's 64 samples is ~0.0075-0.010 of the 0.02 bound (slice/measurements/sub_frame_motion_2026-09-25.json)

seam_margin.criterion: ADR-0002 D1 overlap margin (amendment 2026-09-22, corrected 2026-09-23): WHERE a head continues its shell below the socket boundary curve, that geometry must lie INSIDE the body neck on every frame, so the body wins the depth test below the curve. The slice’s own head has none - it ends at the curve, welded to the body ring (0.000 mm) - and the gate passes vacuously on it. The band measured before the correction was an artefact of reading half the curve; see docs/adr/ADR-0002-correction-2026-09-23-seam-overlap-margin.md
seam_margin.rule: on every frame, every head-shell vertex below the boundary curve has signed distance to the body surface <= -margin_mm (+ = outside the skin), ramped from 0 at the curve to the full margin at ramp_mm below it; tolerance_mm of numerical slack
seam_margin.ring_read: the socket curve is read by MEMBERSHIP of the SOCKET_BOUNDARY vertex group, never by a weight threshold: the weight in that group is the ring ORDER (i/N; export_shot.py refuses non-distinct weights because the order defines the polyline). Reading it as weight > 0.5 keeps one contiguous half-arc — on the contractor's v03, 21 of 42 vertices spanning z 1.1972-1.2108 against the real 1.1813-1.2108 — and everything under that phantom curve looks like head geometry hanging below the seam (2026-09-23: 3622 phantom violations, and 21 of the 45 phantom band vertices were the welded ring itself, which cannot move inside without breaking rest_gap = 0)
seam_margin.excluded: C_HAIR is not measured: hair has free edges, legitimately falls over the shoulders and is replaced by the head technology (ADR-0002 D3). NECK_PROXY and COLLISION_PROXY are not surfaces
seam_margin.radius_note: the region of interest is measured from the curve itself - 1.5x its own radius - not as a fixed distance. A fixed 0.08 m was the real character's neck and excluded everything on the placeholder, whose ring radius is 0.099 m (2026-09-23). Its job is only to keep the chin and the ears out of the band
seam_margin.status: PROVISIONAL — never calibrated against a head that actually has an overlap band: the slice’s head has none, and the 2026-09-22 numbers that suggested these values were measured against a phantom band (corrected 2026-09-23). Calibrate in Phase 1 on the first candidate that brings one
seam_margin.on_fail: SEAM_MARGIN_ERROR, exit 2, worst offenders named with frame, vertex, signed and required distance
